title: Boss: a Monday of other people's Git
summary: A reviewer's fixup in a pushed stack, a force-pushed pull request to re-review, and a repo whose line endings fight everyone.

steps.title: The scene
body: Monday. Your two stacked pull requests got a review comment on the bottom one, Priya force-pushed hers overnight and
wants a second look, and the tools repo makes every Windows user's diff light up red. All three are real repositories
on your machine, each with a bare `origin` where it matters.

steps.title: Fix the bottom of a pushed stack
prompt: In `~/shop` you have two pushed, stacked branches: `stack/1-model` (bottom) and `stack/2-api` (on top of it, checked out). `main` gained a commit on the server.
The reviewer asks for one change in the bottom PR: `src/Coupon.cs` must say `public int Percent; // 1 to 100`.
1. Make the change as a **fixup** of `Add the coupon model`.
2. In one rebase onto the fresh `origin/main`, fold it in and move both branches.
Afterwards each branch still has exactly one commit of its own.

checks.name: stack/1-model: new main plus the fixed model commit
checks.cmd: cd /srv/git/shop.git && test "$(git rev-parse stack/1-model^)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/main)" && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s stack/1-model)" = 'Add the coupon model' && git show stack/1-model:src/Coupon.cs | grep -q '1 to 100'
checks.fail: On the server, `stack/1-model` should be the new `main` plus one commit, `Add the coupon model`, which now has the `1 to 100` comment.

checks.name: stack/2-api: stack/1-model plus the API commit
checks.cmd: cd /srv/git/shop.git && test "$(git rev-parse stack/2-api^)" = "$(git rev-parse stack/1-model)" && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s stack/2-api)" = 'Add the coupon API'
checks.fail: On the server, `stack/2-api` should be the new `stack/1-model` plus `Add the coupon API`. Push both: `git push --force-with-lease origin stack/1-model stack/2-api`.

checks.name: no fixup commit left, local matches the server
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && ! git log --format=%s stack/2-api | grep -q '^fixup!' && test "$(git rev-parse stack/2-api)" = "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git rev-parse stack/2-api)" && ! test -d .git/rebase-merge
checks.fail: A `fixup!` commit is still in the history, a rebase is still running, or the server differs from your branches.

hints: Edit the file, then `git commit -a --fixup="$(git rev-parse stack/1-model)"` on `stack/2-api`.
solution: sed -i 's|public int Percent;|public int Percent; // 1 to 100|' src/Coupon.cs
steps.explain: Three flags in one rebase: `--autosquash` moves the fixup down, `--update-refs` keeps `stack/1-model` pointing at the fixed commit, and the new base pulls in `main`. The fixup could be committed on the top branch because the rebase covers the whole stack.

steps.title: Re-review a force-pushed pull request
prompt: Yesterday you reviewed Priya's `priya/search-sort` (your clone `~/shop` still has that version as `origin/priya/search-sort`). Overnight she force-pushed a v2.
1. Fetch, and find out what changed between v1 and v2 with `git range-diff`.
2. Save the names of the files whose content differs between v1 and v2, one per line, in `~/answers/changed.txt`.
3. Check out her branch locally (same name, tracking the server) at v2, to run it.

checks.name: changed.txt names the file that differs
checks.fail: Only one file differs between v1 and v2. `git diff --name-only 'origin/priya/search-sort@{1}' origin/priya/search-sort` lists it.

checks.name: priya/search-sort is checked out at v2, tracking the server
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git branch --show-current)" = priya/search-sort && test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/v2)" && test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{upstream}')" = origin/priya/search-sort
checks.fail: Check out `priya/search-sort` with `git switch priya/search-sort` after fetching: it should be at v2 and track `origin/priya/search-sort`.

hints: After `git fetch`, `origin/priya/search-sort@{1}` is v1 and `origin/priya/search-sort` is v2.
`git range-diff 'origin/priya/search-sort@{1}...origin/priya/search-sort'` pairs the commits; `=` means unchanged, `!` changed.
steps.explain: The range-diff says commit 1 changed (`!`) and commit 2 did not (`=`), even though both have new hashes: so you only need to re-review the sort change. That is the question every reviewer has after a force-push, answered in one command.

steps.title: One set of rules for every OS
prompt: `~/tools` holds shell scripts, a PowerShell script and an image, committed with whatever line endings people had. `./build.sh` fails with `bad interpreter`.

Write a `.gitattributes` that makes text LF by default, keeps `*.ps1` as CRLF on every machine, and marks `*.png` as binary. Renormalize, commit as `Add line ending rules`, and refresh your working copy so `./build.sh` runs.

checks.name: the stored endings follow the rules
checks.cmd: cd ~/tools && git ls-files --eol build.sh test.sh | grep -c 'i/lf' | grep -qx 2 && git check-attr eol -- deploy.ps1 | grep -q 'eol: crlf' && git check-attr binary -- logo.png | grep -q 'binary: set'
checks.fail: `build.sh` and `test.sh` should be stored with LF, `deploy.ps1` should have `eol=crlf` and `logo.png` should be `binary` (check with `git check-attr -a <file>`).

checks.name: the rules and the renormalized files are committed
checks.cmd: cd ~/tools && git cat-file -e HEAD:.gitattributes && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = 'Add line ending rules' && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
checks.fail: Commit `.gitattributes` and the renormalized files as `Add line ending rules`, leaving a clean tree.

checks.name: build.sh runs and the image is untouched
checks.cmd: cd ~/tools && ./build.sh && test "$(git cat-file -p HEAD:logo.png | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' | cut -c1-16)" = 89504e470d0a1a0a
checks.fail: `./build.sh` still fails (refresh it from the index) or the PNG header lost its CR LF bytes (it must be `binary`).

hints: Three lines: `* text=auto eol=lf`, `*.ps1 text eol=crlf`, `*.png binary`.
`printf '%s\n' '* text=auto eol=lf' '*.ps1 text eol=crlf' '*.png binary' > .gitattributes`, `git add .gitattributes`, `git add --renormalize .`, commit.
`rm build.sh && git restore build.sh` writes it again with LF.
solution: printf '%s\n' '* text=auto eol=lf' '*.ps1 text eol=crlf' '*.png binary' > .gitattributes
steps.explain: `text=auto` lets Git detect binaries, but an explicit `binary` for known formats is cheap insurance: a PNG starts with the bytes `\r\n`, and converting them would corrupt every image. `eol=crlf` for `.ps1` keeps Windows-only tools happy even when the file is edited on a Mac.
